### Observed differences

- The dominant difference is a reversal of execution order between two groups of activities. In the earlier window, A19, A21 and A24 (each present in roughly 3–4 in 10 traces) sat at about one-third of the trace (mean event positions 0.36–0.37), followed by A25 (0.39) and A29 (0.58), with A20, A22 and A23 (present in every trace) at about two-thirds (0.64–0.65). In the later window this is reversed: A20/A22/A23 at about 0.38, A25 at 0.45, A29 at 0.64, and A19/A21/A24 at about 0.67. Every one of the 21 observed pairwise order relations among these eight activities flipped, mostly near-deterministically — e.g., A25 preceded A22 in about 97 in 100 traces before, and A22 precedes A25 in about 97 in 100 after; A29 preceded A23 in 99 in 100 before, A23 precedes A29 in 99 in 100 after. [REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]

- The handovers moved with the blocks. Earlier, A19→A25, A21→A25 and A24→A25 carried about 95, 93 and 97 in 100 of those activities' outgoing transitions; in the later window they run to A30 at similar shares (about 95, 92 and 97 in 100). Conversely, A20→A30, A22→A30 and A23→A30 (about 29–37 in 100) gave way to A20→A25 (37), A22→A25 (28) and A23→A25 (35). A29 now leads mainly to A24, A21 and A19 (about 38/32/28 in 100) instead of A20/A23/A22, and A40 now leads to A22/A20/A23 (about 31/27/24 in 100) instead of A21/A24/A19. Adjacency flips match: A22→A30 and A23→A30 were observed in about 200 of 200 traces earlier and in 1 trace later; A19→A30 and A21→A30 are new and immediate (1 → 65 and 58 traces, at lag 1); A22→A25 and A23→A25 are new (1 → 200 traces, within one to three steps); A21→A25 and A40→A21 all but disappeared (69 → 2 traces each); A40's reach to A25 moved from lag 2 to lags 4–5. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG023, LAG024, LAG027, LAG028, LAG029]

- Participation of these eight activities barely moved (A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 in every trace in both windows; A19 about 31→33 in 100, A21 36→29, A24 36→39), so this is a reordering of existing behaviour, not activities appearing, disappearing or running more often. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]

- A08 became much rarer: it appeared in about 64 in 100 traces earlier versus about 29 in 100 in the later window (mean occurrences per trace about 0.68→0.32), and its remaining occurrences sit later and more variably (mean position about 0.26→0.41). Its dominant outgoing edge to A16 fell from about 93 to 31 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and is now spread over many targets; the upstream A15→A08 handover fell from about 39 to 7 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions; and A08 co-occurred with partners such as A16, A20, A25 and A40 in about 64 in 100 traces before versus about 29 in 100 after, while those partners still occur without it in about 72 in 100. [OCC003, POS001, DIR002, DIR005, REL003, REL005, REL010, REL013, LAG001, LAG005]

- A04, A06 and A10 roughly doubled or tripled their presence (A04 about 7→21 in 100 traces, A06 7→24, A10 9→19) and their outgoing profiles changed: A04 now leads mostly to A46, A15, A44 and A23, and A10's transitions, previously spread almost evenly over many targets, now concentrate on A46 (about 23 in 100), A15 (18) and A22 (13). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]

- Smaller shifts around A14–A16 and A45–A46: A15→A16 rose to about 88 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions (from 61), A16 self-repetitions at lag 2 grew from about 16 to 35 in 100, and A45→A46 moved partly from lag 1 to lag 2 (about 97→84 in 100 at lag 1). [DIR005, LAG015, LAG030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, two blocks of activities exchanged their place in the execution order around an unchanged middle. Earlier the sequence ran A19/A21/A24 → A25 → A29 → A20/A22/A23 → A30; in the later window it runs A20/A22/A23 → A25 → A29 → A19/A21/A24 → A30, with upstream A40 now feeding A22/A20/A23 where it previously fed A21/A24/A19. The reversal is shown directly by relational evidence: all 21 observed pairwise order relations among A19, A21, A24, A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 flipped, each measured on co-occurrence in all 200 traces per window and holding in about 95–100 in 100 of joint appearances in each window; the positional shifts of about 0.3 of the trace agree for all six block members; and the successor changes and adjacency flips line up with the same rewiring. Because participation stayed essentially unchanged, this reads as a reordering of existing behaviour rather than activities becoming optional, new or repeated. The screening comparison supports the pattern as a whole: 94 control-flow items qualified where about 1 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, and each item's difference exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits. Limitations: positions are event positions, not clock times; a few corroborating LAG items rest on a single observation in one window (the order reversals they support are, however, independently established by the full-support REL items); and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample two process variants whose relative frequencies changed rather than a single reordered process — although the near-deterministic single order within each window makes a stable mixture of both orders unlikely. [REL016, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL030, REL031, REL033, REL034, REL036, POS002, POS003, POS006, POS007, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, LAG018, LAG020, LAG022, LAG023]

Other differences: A08 participation fell from about 64 to 29 in 100 traces and its A15→A08→A16 detour largely disappeared, a participation change separate from the reordering; A04, A06 and A10 became roughly two to three times as common with rewired successors; and small shifts occurred around A15/A16 and A45/A46. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, LAG015, LAG030]
